Abstract: Cryptovivipary and vivipary, referred to as (crypto)vivipary, occur across multiple angiosperm lineages and enable embryos to continue developing before dispersal. Yet, this trait raises a fundamental question: how are seed-specific abscisic acid (ABA) responses modulated to support continuous embryonic growth without compromising ABA-dependent vegetative stress tolerance? Here, integrating phylogenomic analyses of independently evolved (crypto)viviparous lineages with spatiotemporal transcriptomics and functional validation, we show that (crypto)vivipary evolved via a convergent “less-is-more” strategy rather than through novel genes or single master loci (e.g., DOG1 ). While upstream hormonal cores (e.g., ABA/GA signaling) are largely conserved, downstream seed desiccation and dormancy effectors are asymmetrically dismantled across cryptoviviparous and viviparous lineages. This remodeling, encompassing 38 shared contracted orthogroups and hundreds of lineage-specific losses, converges on eliminating the execution machinery for seed desiccation tolerance and dormancy maintenance. Consistently, orthologs of the contracted genes are enriched for dry-seed–specific expression and ABA responsiveness in non-(crypto)viviparous species. Furthermore, disrupting representative Arabidopsis orthologs (e.g., SESA1 , TIP3.2 , LEA25 , ECP63 ) recapitulates (crypto)viviparous-like phenotypes, including precocious germination, elevated seed moisture, and in most mutants, compromised storage longevity. Together, our findings demonstrate how structured contraction of terminal seed-specific modules uncouples seed developmental fate from systemic stress signaling, illuminating the molecular architecture of (crypto)vivipary.
Author: Zhao, Kanglu
Source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
Title: Convergent innovation of (crypto)vivipary via asymmetric dismantling of seed desiccation and dormancy machinery

Abstract: Melanoma remains a lethal malignancy with frequent resistance to immune checkpoint blockade therapy. Clinical evidence associates elevated PAK4 expression with poor response to anti-PD-1 treatment in melanoma patients. While tumor-derived exosomes are recognized as key immunosuppressive mediators, the role of PAK4 in regulating exosome secretion to induce immunosuppression remains incompletely understood. Here, we demonstrate that PAK4-mediated phosphorylation of Annexin-A2 (ANXA2) at Ser26 promotes its nuclear-to-cytoplasmic translocation, facilitating the formation of S100A10-ANXA2 heterotetramers that drive multivesicular body docking to the plasma membrane. Furthermore, PAK4 stabilizes synaptotagmin-1 by suppressing Trim21-mediated ubiquitin degradation, enabling SNARE complex assembly for membrane fusion. PAK4-driven exosomes exhibit potent immunosuppressive activity, substantially reducing CD8 + T cell numbers and impairing their function in mouse models. Notably, melanoma cells with high PAK4 expression secrete PD-L1-enriched exosomes that promote systemic immune evasion. In patient-derived xenograft models, pharmacological inhibition of PAK4 attenuates tumor progression and reduces circulating exosomal PD-L1 levels. Our study unveils a dual mechanism through which PAK4 drives exosome-dependent immunosuppression, providing a rationale for combining PAK4 pathway inhibitors with immune checkpoint blockade and offering translational strategies to overcome melanoma immunotherapy resistance.
Author: Zhou, Ruizhi
Source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
Title: PAK4 exacerbates melanoma immunosuppression by promoting exosome release

Abstract: Helping others is an integral part of human sociality, but systematic cross-cultural comparisons of children's helping behavior are rare. Existing work has mainly focused on interactions between adults and children, paying less attention to peer dynamics-which are more relevant in many cultural settings. Here, we report a study of 4- to 9-y-old children's (N = 336) spontaneous helping in 6 highly diverse populations in Latin America, Africa, and Europe (Wichí, Quechua, ≠Akhoe Hai||om, Samburu, Kikuyu, and Germans). In all settings, we observed pairs of same-aged children in an experimental task in which one partner could assist the other by providing either instrumental help or information. Across cultures, children reliably helped their peers by offering either type of help, with the provision of information increasing over age. We found striking commonalities in peer helping in all settings, with only small culture-specific patterns in children's responses. This suggests that helping among children is a universal human behavior which is subtly shaped by local norms and practices.
Author: Zeidler, Henriette
Source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
Title: Children from six cultures reliably help their peers—but in different ways

Abstract: BACKGROUND: Endometrial polyps (EP) can lead to irregular bleeding and infertility in women. The identification of biomarkers associated with EP holds clinical importance. METHODS: Patients who visited the hospital due to abnormal uterine bleeding, endometrial thickening, abnormal menstruation, lower abdominal pain, infertility, or repeated miscarriages were included. Thirty-four patients were diagnosed with EP; 32 patients with no previous history of EP and negative histological results were taken as the control. The expression levels of MPO, ER, PR, MMP2, MMP9, PCNA, and COX2 in the two groups were assessed by immunohistochemistry and western blot. The relationships between MPO, ER, and PR, and clinicopathological characteristics, inflammation, hormones, and glycolipid metabolism of EP patients, were also analyzed. RESULTS: The expression of MPO, ER, MMP2, MMP9, PCNA, and COX2 in the EP group was markedly increased, while that of PR was markedly reduced. In EP tissues, MPO had a positive correlation with ER and a negative correlation with PR. Increased MPO expression was associated with abnormal uterine bleeding, polyp size exceeding 1 cm, endometrial proliferation stage, and higher VAS pain score. Increased ER expression was associated with multiple polyps and larger polyp size. Reduced PR expression was associated with multiple polyps and endometrial secretory phase. In addition, increased MPO expression was associated with increased levels of CRP and PLR and reduced hemoglobin levels. CONCLUSION: MPO and ER in EP are significantly upregulated, while PR is significantly downregulated. Increased MPO expression is associated with elevated inflammatory markers and reduced hemoglobin levels, while ER/PR imbalance is related to multiple polyps and polyp size.
Author: Xu, Xiaoyan
Title: Histological significance of MPO, ER, and PR in endometrial polyps of premenopausal women.

Abstract: Abstract Redox-active ligands are well established for enabling open-shell reactivity in first-row transition-metal catalysis. Despite the privileged role of 2,2′-bipyridine (bpy) ligands in homogeneous catalysis, bpy-supported half-sandwich organoiron complexes have remained essentially unexplored. Here we report the synthesis and characterization of a previously elusive family of half-sandwich iron complexes, (η5-C5Me5)Fe(bpy)(X) (X = Cl, Br), and their application in catalytic carbene transfer. Single-electron reduction affords a low-valent 17-electron complex best described as having a predominantly Fe(II)/bpy•– electronic structure. In contrast to classical (η5-C5H5)Fe(CO)2 (Fp)-type iron systems that mainly engage in two-electron reactivity, the redox-active bpy–(η5-C5Me5)Fe platform undergoes homolytic bond activation, including halogen-atom transfer from benzylic gem-dihalides. Leveraging this open-shell reactivity, catalytic cyclopropanation of styrenes and related alkenes was achieved using gem-dihalides as carbene precursors and manganese as terminal reductant. These findings establish bpy-supported half-sandwich iron complexes as a structurally tunable, non-heme platform for catalytic carbene transfer reactivity.
Author: Liu, Gang
Source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Title: Redox-Active Bipyridine–Iron Half-Sandwich Complexes for Catalytic Carbene Transfer

Abstract: Abstract Neutrophils are the most abundant circulating leukocytes in the innate immune system. Primary neutrophils comprise multiple distinct subtypes that regulate antimicrobial defense and inflammatory diseases. Current fluorescent probes for imaging neutrophils cannot distinguish between activation mechanisms. In this work, we present dual enzyme- and metabolite-activatable fluorogenic probes that are selective for activated neutrophils prone to inflammatory responses. Our probes integrate, within a single scaffold, two neutrophil-associated activation mechanisms, that is, cathepsin G–mediated cleavage of FRET substrates and fluorophore oxidation by hypochlorous acid. This chemical design allows the selective identification of activated neutrophils over other immune cells from peripheral blood of human donors. This strategy provides a unique approach for in situ analysis of neutrophil heterogeneity in multiple pathologies, including different inflammatory diseases.
Author: Iijima, Kohei
Source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Title: Activity-Guided Identification of Pro-inflammatory Neutrophils with Dual Enzyme- and Metabolite-Activatable Fluorescent Probes

Abstract: Abstract Direct air capture (DAC) of CO2 has emerged as an indispensable negative emission technology, yet current sorbents remain constrained by the persistent trade-off between intrinsic capture capacity and regeneration energy alongside the extrinsic challenge of atmospheric moisture inhibition. Herein, engineering of crystalline and thermally stable alkali metal pyrazolate coordination polymers (MRPyr) is established as a novel paradigm for the metal–ligand cooperative (MLC), moisture-gated, and highly selective capture of CO2 from ambient air streams. While inert in low-humidity air, activation of solid-state MRPyr by atmospheric moisture unlocks exceptional CO2-capture capacities (7.4–9.2 mmol/g) and realizes a substantial CO2:pyrazolate stoichiometry (0.83–0.89) through formation of metal carbamate (MRCarbamate). To elucidate the operative mechanism, crystallographic snapshots and in/ex situ spectroscopic analyses unveil that MLC hydration of KMePyr yielding KMePyr·H2O triggers a substantial structural rearrangement from a compact double-ladder chain into an expanded zig-zag architecture. This moisture-gated transformation relieves steric shielding and unleashes intrinsic nucleophilicity of pyrazolate ligands to initiate CO2 capture via a thermodynamically favored displacement of bound water. Finally, quantitative regeneration of MRPyr from CO2-saturated MRCarbamate adducts and demonstrated multiple-cycle recyclability under a temperature-vacuum swing adsorption process position the robust MRPyr platform as a paradigm-shifting class of sorbents for sustainable DAC applications.
Author: Yu, Tsu-Chieh
Source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Title: Engineering Metal Pyrazolate Coordination Polymers for Highly Selective Direct Air Capture via Metal–Ligand Cooperativity and Moisture-Gated Mechanism

Abstract: Abstract Natural products have been paramount in inspiring novel chemistry as well as providing therapeutic agents and chemical tools for biological applications. A recently emerging class of natural products, the thio/seleno-imidazoles (TSIs), contains C–S or C–Se bonds that are installed by nonheme iron sulfoxide and selenoxide synthases (NHISSs). These TSIs, which include ergothioneine, are ubiquitous, but little is known about the broader TSI chemical space or co-occurrence with other biosynthetic enzymes. Here, we use NHISSs as a bioinformatic hook to identify a widespread family of biosynthetic gene clusters that encode a combination of NHISS and ATP-grasp enzymes. This search strategy enabled the discovery of two 2-thiohistidine-containing dipeptide natural products, one of which we isolated from the original microbial host. Structural and biochemical analyses of the corresponding biosynthetic enzymes revealed a novel NHISS active site architecture and an ATP-grasp enzyme with unprecedented substrate selectivity for 2-thiohistidine. Together, these results expand the known enzymology and distribution of TSIs and establish 2-thiohistidine as a biosynthetically encoded building block, enabling future discovery and functional investigation into this new natural product family.
Author: Marissa L. Abbott
Source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Subfield: Renewable Energy, Sustainability and the Environment
Title: Widespread Biosynthesis of Thiohistidine Dipeptides in Bacteria

Abstract: Abstract Magnetoresistance (MR), a cornerstone for quantum materials and quantum devices, is usually symmetric (sometimes antisymmetric) under magnetic field reversal. Here, we report a chirality-induced one-way magnetoresistance (ChiMR) in gold nanocrystals, where MR is strongly amplified, up to several tens of fold, under a small magnetic field (30 mT), but vanished under the opposite field, yielding a diode-like magnetic response at room temperature. The preferred direction of ChiMR is dictated by the nanocrystal handedness, which reverses for opposite enantiomers. We show that chirality and a magnetic field jointly reshape the nanocrystal surface potential, giving rise to ChiMR. This effect demonstrates that chirality can break the conventional symmetry of magnetotransport, introducing a new degree of freedom for controlling the magnetic response. Our findings establish ChiMR as a distinct magnetotransport phenomenon, identify chiral nanocrystals as a platform for directional quantum electronic functionalities, and open new opportunities for magnetic field-mediated control in chiral systems across electronics, catalysis, and biological processes.
Author: Wu, Fengxia
Source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Subfield: Atomic and Molecular Physics, and Optics
Title: Chirality-Induced One-Way Magnetoresistance in Gold Nanocrystals

Abstract: Abstract The combination of site-specific incorporation of 19F-labeled unnatural amino acids (UAAs) and 19F nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy is a powerful strategy for investigating protein structure, dynamics, and interactions. However, commonly used 19F-containing UAAs often suffer from narrow chemical shift dispersion and low sensitivity to environmental or protein conformational changes, especially in complex cellular conditions. Herein, we report a 19F-labeled unnatural amino acid, monofluoromethylphenylalanine (mfmF, CH2F-Phe), which displays superior spectroscopic properties for both in vitro and in-cell 19F NMR studies. Using genetic code expansion, CH2F-Phe was efficiently site-specifically incorporated into two model proteins light-oxygen-voltage sensing domain 2 (LOV2) and Calmodulin (CaM). Compared to trifluoromethylphenylalanine (CF3-Phe), CH2F-Phe exhibits broader 19F chemical shift dispersion and markedly enhanced sensitivity to environmental changes. Using this synthesized 19F NMR probe, we successfully achieved sensitive detection of the light-induced conformational transition of LOV2 in vitro. Furthermore, CH2F-Phe-incorporated CaM displayed remarkably sensitive and substantially larger 19F chemical shift differences (>1.0–2.0 ppm) between the apo- and Ca2+-bound states compared to CF3-Phe-labeled CaM, enabling the detection of previously unresolved intermediate states during Ca2+-dependent conformational transitions in living cells. Collectively, CH2F-Phe serves as an invaluable probe to characterize protein dynamics and interactions.
Author: Shi, Pan
Source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Title: Monofluoromethylphenylalanine: A Sensitive 19F Probe for Protein Conformational Dynamics In Vitro and in Cells

Abstract: Undernutrition and infectious diseases pose a double threat to child survival, especially in areas with a high malnutrition burden and low vaccination coverage. In this study, we evaluated whether distributing preventive small-quantity lipid-based nutrient supplements (SQ-LNS) alongside routine immunization services may increase vaccine uptake in a pediatric, pragmatic, cluster-randomized controlled trial in northern Nigeria. Twenty geographically defined clusters across two Local Government Areas were randomized 1:1 to the NutriVax strategy (intervention) or standard National Program of Immunization (NPI) services (control). NutriVax provided a monthly ration of SQ-LNS to children aged 6-23 months after routine NPI delivery at primary healthcare centers. The primary outcome was coverage of the first dose of measles-containing vaccine (MCV1) verified by vaccination card among children aged 12-23 months, assessed in an endline population-based household cross-sectional survey 12 months after conducting a similar baseline survey. The endline survey included 1,604 children (801 control, 803 NutriVax); 48% of children surveyed in intervention clusters had ever received SQ-LNS. The odds of receiving card-verified MCV1 were two times higher in the NutriVax arm than in the control arm (odds ratio = 2.08, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.30-3.35, P = 0.004). The difference-in-differences, cluster conditional analysis indicated a 20.1 percentage-point (pp) increase in MCV1 coverage from baseline (95% CI: 13.7-26.5 pp, P < 0.0001) relative to the control arm. Co-delivering SQ-LNS with routine immunization substantially improved card-verified MCV1 uptake, supporting a scalable strategy to make progress toward targets set by the World Health Organization's Immunization Agenda 2030 in similar settings. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06387511 .
Author: Cazes, Cécile
Title: Small quantity lipid-based nutritional supplementation and measles vaccination coverage in children aged 6−23 months: a pragmatic cluster-randomized trial

Abstract: Abstract Chemical stressors in environmental and clinical settings can alter conjugative plasmid transfer, which is a key process driving antibiotic resistance dissemination. However, predicting these effects across chemically diverse compounds is challenging. Here, we compiled and curated data on the effect of chemical stressors on RP4 plasmid transfer, extracting compound identity, concentration, conjugation frequency, and experimental metadata from 73 in vitro studies. Chemicals were characterized by functional use categories and molecular descriptors, including physicochemical properties, MACCS keys, Morgan fingerprints, and extended descriptors from the OCHEM platform (AlvaDesc, Dragon 7, and 3D-shape descriptors). An exhaustive evaluation of 1022 feature set combinations across 3066 models showed that chemical concentration alone provides no meaningful predictive signal (Q2ext <0), whereas integrating Morgan fingerprints substantially improves predictive performance. The best-performing model combined concentration, Morgan fingerprints, and experimental conditions using extreme gradient boosting (XGB), achieving Q2ext = 0.373 on a held-out compound-aware test set and a median Q2ext of 0.319 within the defined applicability domain across 20 independent splits. SHAP analysis revealed that Morgan fingerprints account for 69% of total predictive weight, with quaternary ammonium compounds and long-chain alkyl structures associated with inhibition of conjugation and sulfonamide and amine-containing compounds associated with promotion. These results demonstrate that chemical structural features provide critical information for predicting the chemical modulation of conjugative plasmid transfer. This work highlights that combining chemically informed descriptors with machine learning (ML) anticipates chemical contributions to antibiotic resistance dissemination, providing a scalable framework for the prioritization and risk assessment of chemicals.
Author: Ana Rey Sogo
Title: Predicting Chemical Stressor Effects on Conjugative Plasmid Transfer Rates Using Machine Learning

Abstract: Abstract Despite loss of responsiveness to exogenous leptin in obesity, endogenous leptin continues to restrain feeding, although the neural substrates that remain sensitive and mediate this effect remain unknown. Combining spatial transcriptomics with single-nucleus RNA sequencing in mice with diet-induced obesity (DIO), we here show that while most hypothalamic leptin receptor ( Lepr )-positive neurons minimally respond to elevated leptin, a single subpopulation defined by glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor ( Glp1r ) co-expression retains robust leptin sensitivity. These Lepr + /Glp1r + neurons project onto and inhibit orexigenic Agrp neurons. Lepr deletion from Lepr + /Glp1r + neurons blocks the anorectic effect of exogenous leptin, reinstates hyperphagic responses normally suppressed in DIO, amplifies the obesogenic response to palatable diet, and unexpectedly attenuates hypothalamic microglial activation – a hallmark of DIO previously attributed to diet rather than leptin signaling. Hence, preserved leptin responses by a single neuronal population in the hypothalamus limit hyperphagia and weight gain, among other responses, during obesity.
Author: Dylan Matthew Belmont-Rausch
Title: Leptin-sensitive hypothalamic Lepr+/Glp1r+ neurons limit hyperphagia and weight gain in diet-induced obesity

Abstract: Concerns about climate risk suggest it should affect risk assessment and pricing of corporate securities, particularly for firms facing potential regulatory restrictions. Employing a shock to expected climate regulations, we find support for this hypothesis given our evidence that climate regulatory risks causally affect bond credit ratings and yield spreads. Moreover, a structural credit model indicates the increased spreads for high carbon issuers, especially those located in stricter regulatory environments, derive from changes in firms’ asset volatilities rather than asset values, highlighting that regulatory uncertainty affects security pricing. The results have important implications for corporate decisions, portfolio management, and policymaking.
Author: Seltzer, Lee
Title: Climate regulatory risks and corporate bonds

Abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether residency program unionization was associated with differences in resident well-being, learning environment, and mistreatment during the COVID-19 pandemic. BACKGROUND: Resident unionization increased following the COVID-19 pandemic, driven by concerns regarding well-being and working conditions. However, evidence regarding the impact of unionization on resident outcomes remains limited. METHODS: This difference-in-differences (DiD) study used data from a national survey administered to general surgery residents following the American Board of Surgery In-Training Examination from 2020 to 2023. We compared responses obtained before the pandemic (January 2020) and during the pandemic (January 2021), with 2022-2023 data included in sensitivity analyses. Residents from 310 programs (94.5% of eligible programs) were included, of which 30 (9.7%) were unionized. Outcomes included resident well-being (burnout, thoughts of attrition, and suicidal ideation), learning environment (duty-hour violations, protected educational time, and program responsiveness to resident concerns), and mistreatment. RESULTS: A total of 13,539 responses were analyzed (response rates: 85.5% in 2020 and 81.2% in 2021). Unionization was not significantly associated with changes in burnout (DiD P=0.06), thoughts of attrition (DiD P=0.83), or suicidal ideation (DiD P=0.25). No significant differences were observed in duty-hour violations (DiD P=0.56) or protected educational time (DiD P=0.51). By 2023, nonunionized programs showed greater improvement in duty-hour violations (DiD P=0.003) and protected educational time (DiD P<0.001). Unionized programs demonstrated a transient improvement in program responsiveness to resident concerns during the initial pandemic period (DiD P=0.04), which did not persist by 2023 (DiD P=0.53). No differences were observed for mistreatment measures. CONCLUSIONS: Unionization was not associated with improvements in resident well-being, the learning environment, or mistreatment during the pandemic, with the exception of a transient improvement in program responsiveness to resident concerns. These findings suggest that unionization alone may not be sufficient to protect resident wellness during periods of systemic stress.
Author: Alexa J. Hughes
Title: Well-being, Learning Environment, and Mistreatment Among Unionized Versus Nonunionized Surgery Residents During the COVID-19 Pandemic

Abstract: Abstract Accurate segmentation of brain tumors in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is crucial for effective treatment planning and post-treatment monitoring. However, challenges such as intensity inhomogeneity, low-contrast boundaries, and highly irregular tumor morphology significantly complicate this task. In this work, we introduce a two-stage hybrid framework that integrates a convolutional U-Net for coarse tumor localization with a morphological Laplacian-enhanced active contour model for precise boundary refinement. While the U-Net is trained using bimodal input (FLAIR + T1ce) to generate reliable initial masks, all refinement steps and final performance evaluations are conducted exclusively on single-modality FLAIR images—ensuring clinical simplicity and robustness. The proposed active contour incorporates a novel local fitting term based on morphological Laplacian operators, which capture structural transitions and enhance edge sensitivity. An adaptive weighting function dynamically balances the influence of local and global intensity information during contour evolution, improving resilience to noise and intensity variations without compromising computational efficiency. When evaluated on the BraTS 2020 dataset, the proposed method achieves a Dice coefficient of 96.48% ± 1.57%, a Jaccard index of 93.43% ± 2.92%, and a sensitivity of 97.01% ± 1.69%. Comparative experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms both classical active contour models and contemporary deep learning architectures in whole-tumor segmentation from FLAIR-only MRI. The source code will be made publicly available upon acceptance.
Author: Mohammad Ali Kazemi
Title: Segmentation of brain tumors using a morphological Laplacian-enhanced active contour model on MRI

Abstract: The present investigation centers on the formulation and characterization of a light-cured nanohybrid dental composite, which incorporates a newly-proposed hybrid filler system composed of barium glass microparticles alongside surface-engineered zirconia nanoparticles. Notably, scandia- and yttria-stabilized zirconia nanoparticles (ScYSZ NPs) are introduced here for the first time within a methacrylate-based resin matrix. To improve interfacial compatibility, these nanoparticles were treated with γ-methacryloxypropyltrimethoxysilane (MPS), and three distinct dispersion techniques were systematically evaluated to secure a uniform particle distribution. Following identification of the optimal processing route, surface-modified ScYSZ (F-ScYSZ) was loaded at 1, 2.5, and 5 wt.% into a base resin already containing 48 wt.% barium glass. The resulting composites underwent thorough characterization through FT-IR, XRD, MTT and FE-SEM analysis. Mechanical response was quantified through three-point bending tests and Vickers indentation, whereas polymerization shrinkage was determined in line with ISO 17304 guidelines. The analyses verified the successful attachment of MPS moieties onto the nanoparticle surfaces and confirmed the retention of the non-transformable tetragonal (t′) polymorph within the ScYSZ structure. Incorporation of F-ScYSZ at 1 and 2.5 wt.% brought about substantial gains in mechanical performance; the best-performing formulation at 2.5 wt.% delivered a flexural strength of 134.33 MPa, an elastic modulus of 4.58 GPa, and a microhardness of 39.4 HV. At the 5 wt.% level, however, observable particle agglomeration occurred, which was accompanied by a pronounced deterioration in overall properties. Meanwhile, a consistent drop in polymerization shrinkage was noted with increasing filler loading. A side-by-side comparison against commercially available resin‑based composites reveals that the newly developed ScYSZ-reinforced nanohybrid achieves an attractive trade-off between enhanced mechanical strength and lower volumetric shrinkage, underscoring its viability as a high-performance flowable material for restorative dentistry applications.
Author: Zendehdel, Elias
Title: Enhanced mechanical properties and reduced polymerization shrinkage in a light-cured flowable dental nanocomposite via incorporation of silane-functionalized ScYSZ nanoparticles

Abstract: Bottled food packaging may pose operational challenges for older adults due to age-related declines in physical strength, joint mobility, and sensory perception. However, limited research has systematically examined how different packaging usability attributes influence user satisfaction and dissatisfaction. This study investigates operability-related design attributes of bottled food packaging for older consumers using a mixed-methods approach. Semi-structured interviews were first conducted to identify common operational difficulties and generate candidate attributes. A two-round Delphi consultation with experts was then used to refine and validate the attribute system. Finally, a Kano-model questionnaire survey involving 385 older adults was conducted to evaluate how the presence or absence of specific attributes affects user satisfaction. The results identified 27 usability-related attributes across five dimensions: functionality, reliability, usability, proficiency, and creativity. Basic operational and safety-related attributes were mainly classified as Must-be or One-dimensional attributes, indicating that their absence strongly increases dissatisfaction. In contrast, innovation-related attributes were primarily categorized as Attractive attributes, contributing to satisfaction when present but not causing dissatisfaction when absent. These findings reveal an asymmetric satisfaction–dissatisfaction mechanism in older adults’ evaluation of packaging usability and provide design implications for developing ageing-friendly bottled food packaging.
Author: Jian, Xinyi
Title: Prioritizing usability attributes in bottled food packaging for older consumers using the Kano model

Abstract: Abstract The structural-property relationships are key in the study of the physicochemical behavior of pharmaceuticals. The degree-based topological indices available through molecular graph theory are used to investigate the structure-property analysis of selected antimycotic agents in a quantitative way in this work. The molecular graphs of ten antimycotic agents were constructed, and several degree-based indices including $$M^o_1(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$M^o_2(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$F^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$Y^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$S^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$G^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$P^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$HM^\alpha _1(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$HM^\alpha _2(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , and $$HF^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$ were computed to describe their structural characteristics. To enhance descriptive reliability, this study introduces a novel integration of degree-based topological descriptors with comprehensive multivariate statistical techniques—combining linear regression, correlation profiling, and dimensionality reduction to evaluate structural-property dependencies. Statistical methods were applied to examine the connection between molecular structure and various physicochemical properties, including density, boiling point, enthalpy of vaporization, refractive index, molar refractivity, polarizability, molecular volume, surface tension, and atomic mass. The strength of the associations between topological descriptors and physicochemical parameters were analyzed using regression analysis, descriptive statistics, Pearson analysis, and Spearman analysis of correlation. The accuracy of the fitted regression models was quantitatively evaluated for all parameters and showed to be property-dependent. The range of the standard model error metrics were: $$\textrm{MAE} = 0.0234$$ –161.7920 and $$\textrm{RMSE} = 0.0298$$ –262.6852 which scale directly with the magnitude of the target physicochemical properties. Furthermore, Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation yielded cross-validated performance metrics spanning $$Q^2_{\textrm{LOO}} = -2.1417$$ to 0.3514, with associated errors bounded by $$\mathrm {LOOCV\text {-}MAE} = 0.0320$$ to 191.2633 and $$\mathrm {LOOCV\text {-}RMSE} = 0.0371$$ to 304.5087. Moreover, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was applied to reduce data dimensionality and identify the most informative descriptors. These findings indicate that a number of topological indices have strong positive correlations with significant physicochemical characteristics, especially those of boiling point, molar refractivity, molecular volume, and atomic mass. Among descriptors that were examined, the most consistent correlations with physicochemical properties of antimycotic agents are observed in $$M^o_1(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$M^o_2(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , and $$HF^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , where $$M^o_2(\Upsilon ^o)$$ achieved strong descriptive performance for polarizability ( $$R^2 = 0.989$$ , $$\textrm{RMSE} = 22.8565$$ , $$\textrm{MAE} = 17.7267$$ ).. The analysis of the results of PCA indicates that the first two principal components cover about 82 percent of the total variance and, therefore, the cumulative structural and physicochemical descriptors are effective in distinguishing the targeted compounds. Overall, the results indicate that degree-based topological indices are reliable descriptor of the physicochemical behavior of antimycotic agents and serve as effective tools in computational drug development and structure-property prediction.
Author: Asim, Muhammad
Title: Exploratory QSPR analysis of physicochemical properties of selected antifungal agents using topological indices

Abstract: This quasi-experimental study examined whether a school volleyball unit based on the Step-Game-Approach model combined with explicit life skills teaching (SGA + LS) was associated with changes in technical-tactical performance, life skills, motivation, and perception of success. Eighty-eight students aged 10–12 years participated in a quasi-experimental repeated-measures design with three groups: SGA + LS, direct instruction, and control. The intervention comprised 18 Physical Education classes. Outcomes were assessed before and/or after the intervention using IAD-VB, Life Skills Scale for Sport, Behavioral Regulation in Sport Questionnaire, and Perception of Success Questionnaire. Generalized Estimating Equations tested group, time, and group×time effects. Significant group × time interactions that remained significant after false discovery rate correction were observed for goal setting, Wald χ²(2) = 11.875, pFDR=0.009, time management, Wald χ²(2) = 10.203, pFDR=0.014, and communication, Wald χ²(2) = 7.538, pFDR=0.044. All technical-tactical outcomes showed significant adjusted interactions, Wald χ²(2) = 10.764–60.676, pFDR≤0.012, with both volleyball-specific conditions showing improvements across several outcomes. At post-test, SGA + LS showed higher decision-making than control, whereas SGA + LS and direct instruction did not differ significantly after Holm adjustment. For motivational regulation, significant adjusted interactions remained for identified regulation, global intrinsic motivation, goal achievement, stimulating experiences, and knowledge mastery, pFDR≤0.021. No adjusted group × time effect was observed for perceptions of success. Overall, the findings indicate selective rather than uniform associations between SGA + LS and technical-tactical, psychosocial, and motivational outcomes in school Physical Education.
Author: Carolinne Silva Gonçalves
Subfield: Physical Therapy, Sports Therapy and Rehabilitation
Title: SGA-based volleyball teaching with explicit life skills instruction is associated with technical-tactical, psychosocial, and motivational improvements in school students

Abstract: Abstract Interdisciplinary clinical boards (ICB) on chronic inflammatory diseases discuss complicated and multidisciplinary cases with inflammatory conditions among experts in their discipline. Medically specialized large language models (LLMs) are finding increasingly widespread use among physicians to answer clinical questions. LLMs offer the potential to close the gap between rapidly expanding medical knowledge and limited time of physicians by providing evidence-based summaries to clinical questions and enable “real-time” literature search. However, it is unclear if LLMs can be implemented in clinical routine of ICB. In this prospective study, 100 consecutive real-world cases were discussed in our ICB. Each case was first discussed independently of the LLM and a preliminary recommendation was documented. The clinical question was then entered in the LLM “OpenEvidence”, the answer was reviewed by the board with the opportunity to add aspects not previously raised, and the recommendation was subsequently confirmed as final. Each participating expert evaluated the answer of the LLM using a questionnaire comprising eight Likert scale (1–5) items and one free-text item. Two physicians, blinded to each other, additionally evaluated outputs for their agreement with the board’s decision. The same cases were evaluated after prompt optimization at two different time points. The 100 discussed cases resulted in 759 rater-case evaluations. A mean of 2.3 specialties were directly involved in each case. The highest score was achieved by the item “OpenEvidence provided clinically relevant information for this case.” (4.06). Recommendation for future use achieved a mean score of 3.95. Complete agreement of the LLM answer with the final recommendation of the ICB was rated in 40.2% and 50.5% of all evaluable cases ( n = 97) by the two raters. When restricted to consensus cases, i.e. cases rated identically by both raters ( n = 62 of 97), complete agreement was 51.6%. Outputs after prompt optimization tended to be associated with higher agreement, but did not reach statistical significance. Outputs were not stable over time. The integration of OpenEvidence into an ICB was feasible and was perceived as useful by the participating specialists, with partial or complete concordance with the final board recommendation in the majority of evaluable cases. As the study did not assess patient outcomes, clinical harm or hallucinations, no conclusions on patient safety can be drawn. The LLM was naturally limited by the information provided in the prompt. Inadequate questions or missing information led to suboptimal answers, highlighting the importance of identifying and including relevant information beforehand. Expert oversight remains essential. Model drift of LLMs may outweigh prompt optimization.
Author: Ronicke, Moritz
Title: Feasibility and expert evaluation of a medical large language model in an interdisciplinary clinical board

Abstract: Abstract Accurate estimation of fast, slow, and average shear-wave velocities (Vs Fast , Vs Slow , and Vs Average ) is important for evaluating reservoir anisotropy, fracture networks, and stress regimes. In this study, multivariate statistical regression and artificial neural network (ANN) models were developed and compared to predict these velocity components in a well from the Sarvak Formation, Zagros Basin, Iran. The initial dataset comprised 3,234 depth points, of which 2,264 valid points were retained after data preprocessing and normalization. Compressional-wave velocity (Vp), neutron porosity (NPHI), and bulk density (RHOB) were used as input variables. For the statistical models, 70% of the data were used for calibration and 30% for testing, whereas the ANN employed a feedforward backpropagation architecture trained using the Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm, with 70, 15, and 15% of the data allocated to training, validation, and testing, respectively. The statistical models achieved test-set R² values of 0.769129, 0.616225, and 0.725904 for Vs fast , Vs slow and Vs Average , respectively, while the corresponding ANN models achieved R² values of 0.786769, 0.641601, and 0.727609. The ANN therefore provided modest improvements over statistical regression, with the largest improvement observed for Vs Fast and Vs slow . Minor discrepancies at lower velocity ranges may reflect local geological complexities, including intense fracturing. Overall, the proposed approach, particularly the ANN models, provides a practical indirect method for estimating shear-wave velocity components from conventional well logs and may support reservoir characterization where direct dipole-shear measurements are unavailable.
Author: Teymouri, Hamed
Title: Prediction of fast, slow, and average shear-wave velocities from well logs using artificial neural networks and statistical regression

Abstract: Abstract A method for the direct synthesis of 3,3-difluoro-9-azatricyclo[3.3.1.02,4]nonanes via a (5 + 2) cycloaddition between a gem-difluorocyclopropene and an oxidopyridinium ion is reported. This approach furnishes the products in moderate to good yields, with exclusive exo-selectivity and broad substrate compatibility. Its synthetic utility is further demonstrated by a gram-scale reaction and derivatization studies.
Author: Liu, Jing
Title: Regio- and Diastereo-Controlled (5 + 2) Cycloaddition of gem -Difluorocyclopropenes and Oxidopyridinium Ions

Abstract: Fractionation of lignocellulosic biomass is important for efficient utilization of both lignin and carbohydrates. Conventional one-pot reductive catalytic fractionation (RCF) can effectively depolymerize lignin, but challenges remain in balancing lignin monomer yield, carbohydrate retention, and external H 2 demand, as well as in separating the heterogeneous catalyst from carbohydrate-rich solids. Herein, a decoupled route for corn stover valorization was developed. Mild continuous-flow methanol extraction was first used to obtain lignin fragments while preserving the carbohydrate-rich solids. The extracted lignin fragments were subsequently subjected to formic-acid-assisted catalytic hydrogenolysis to produce lignin monomers. The extraction conditions were optimized to balance lignin-fragment recovery and carbohydrate preservation. Subsequently, the extracted lignin fragments were hydrogenolyzed under H 2 and H 2 -free atmosphere. Under optimal extraction conditions, yield of lignin fragments reaches 17.3 ± 0.5 wt%, while the carbohydrate retention remains above 95%. The lignin fragments can preserve a part of chemical structures in raw lignin, while carbohydrate-rich solids retain cellulose I. In the subsequent hydrogenolysis step, the addition of 10% formic acid gives a lignin monomer yield of 21.0 wt% without external H 2 . Compared with one-pot RCF, the decoupled route reduces the monomer yield by 8.1 percentage points, but makes carbohydrate retention increase from 24.1% to over 95%. The work could provide a competitive process-design option for high-efficiency utilization of lignocellulosic biomass.
Author: Meng, Xiangle
Title: Mild continuous-flow methanol extraction coupled with formic acid assisted catalytic hydrogenolysis of corn stover

Abstract: Social prescribing (SP) addresses social determinants of health by linking patients in general practice to community-based, non-clinical services. Despite positive attitudes among general practitioners (GPs), uptake remains limited, and little is known about how SP is interpreted and applied in everyday clinical practice, particularly in contexts where SP is not yet formally embedded in routine primary care. The aim of this study was to explore how SP is understood, negotiated, and applied in general practice, and identify factors influencing its uptake. A qualitative exploratory study conducted in Danish general practice, embedded in a structured SP model implemented in a primary care setting. Data were generated through participant observations in GP cluster meetings, clinical consultations, and project meetings, as well as semi-structured interviews with 15 GPs conducted 1 year after implementation. Data were analysed using thematic analysis inspired by Graneheim and Lundman. Six themes were identified: (1) SP as a negotiated expansion of the medical mandate, (2) the target group as a product of clinical reasoning and moral judgement, (3) younger patients as a blind spot in GPs’ construction of SP candidacy, (4) relational access as a precondition for SP, (5) sustaining SP as a workable clinical practice, and (6) legitimacy of the SP approach is grounded in patient-centred ethics rather than system efficiency. SP is not enacted as a standardized model but as a mediated and negotiated practice. Uptake depends on how GPs construct candidacy, interpret needs, negotiate boundaries, and assess patients’ capacity to engage. These findings highlight SP as a situated practice embedded in primary care dynamics.
Author: Jeanette Wassar Kirk
Title: “More than medicine — but when?” A qualitative study of how general practitioners assess, negotiate, and apply social prescribing in clinical practice

Abstract: Objective: To evaluate the surgical management of feline vertebral fractures and luxations, with emphasis on neurological recovery. Methods: Cats that underwent surgical management of vertebral fractures and luxations, without prior neurological disease, were retrospectively enrolled in this observational study from March 1, 2012, to December 31, 2024. Collected data included signalment, vertebral injury characterization, surgical technique, postoperative reduction, modified Frankel score, and urinary incontinence progression, outcome, and complications from clinical/radiographic follow-up and telephone survey. Descriptive statistics were used to describe outcomes. Results: 30 cats met the inclusion criteria. Injury locations were lumbar (n = 16), thoracic (9), lumbosacral (4), and cervical (1). Preoperative modified Frankel scores were grade 3 (n = 12), grade 4 (8), grade 2 (4), grade 5 (2), and grade 1 (1). Surgical stabilization techniques primarily involved polymethylmethacrylate with screws (n = 18) or pins (9). At 8 weeks postoperatively, 28 cats were ambulatory. In the long term, 23 cats fully recovered. Grade 5 cats did not show neurological improvement. Among the 28 long-term ambulatory cats, 6 had persistent proprioceptive ataxia and all of these had T3-L3 neuroanatomical lesions. Urinary incontinence persisted in 4 cats. Owner assessment of long-term neurological recovery was good or excellent in 27 of 29 cats. Conclusions: Surgical management was associated with favorable neurological recovery, even when surgery was delayed or postoperative reduction was incomplete. Clinical Significance: In cats with vertebral fractures or luxations, surgical management should be considered an effective option when spinal instability or cord compression is present, providing that nociception is preserved.
Author: Severac, Lucas
Source: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
Title: Most cats with a spinal fracture or luxation recover locomotion within 8 weeks of surgery
